item.title: NAFDAC destroys N8bn fake, banned products in North-Central
item.description: By Edwin Philip, Lafia The National Agency for Food and Drug Administration and Control (NAFDAC) has seized and destroyed fake, adulterated, expired and banned products worth more than ₦8 billion across North-Central Nigeria. The Director-General of NAFDAC, Prof. Mojisola Adeyeye, disclosed this on Thursday in Lafia, Nasarawa State, saying the products were confiscated from manufacturing facilities, sales outlets, markets and motor parks across the zone. Adeyeye, who was represented by a Deputy Director of the agency in the zone, Joseph Edor, said the bulk of the destroyed products comprised banned alcoholic beverages packaged in sachets and containers smaller than 200 millilitres. She explained that the restriction on alcoholic beverages in sachets and glass bottles below 200ml was introduced because their affordability, availability and portability made them susceptible to abuse, particularly among young people and underage schoolchildren. According to her, early exposure to alcohol can affect brain development and damage vital organs, including the liver and kidneys. “Research has shown that early exposure to alcohol affects the brain and other vital organs such as the liver and kidneys,” she said. She added that alcohol consumption among children could contribute to impaired brain development, poor academic performance, reduced productivity and other health complications. Adeyeye said NAFDAC was established under Decree No. 19 of 1993, as amended, with the responsibility of protecting public health by ensuring that regulated products manufactured, imported, distributed and sold in Nigeria meet the required quality and safety standards. She said the ban on certain alcoholic beverages and the subsequent enforcement operations were aimed at curbing abuse, addiction and associated health risks. Other items seized during the operations included expired and counterfeit medicines, as well as adulterated and unwholesome food products and cosmetics. The director-general commended law enforcement agencies, sister agencies and other stakeholders for supporting NAFDAC’s operations through intelligence sharing and the provision of security. The Nasarawa State Coordinator of NAFDAC, Dr. Gyani Stephen, said the exercise was intended to protect public health rather than harm traders or businesses. She warned dealers in counterfeit and banned products to desist from the practice, adding that the agency would take legal action against offenders. In a goodwill message, the Nasarawa State Commander of the National Drug Law Enforcement Agency, Daniel Saidu, represented by Yakubu Awoh, commended NAFDAC for its efforts to protect lives through the seizure and destruction of expired and counterfeit products. item.title: Obi promises emergency measures on security, corruption, poverty
item.description: Presidential candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), Mr Peter Obi, has promised emergency measures to tackle insecurity, corruption, hunger and poverty, if elected. Obi made the promise on Thursday during an interactive town hall meeting with a large crowd of supporters across party lines in Abakaliki. The former Anambra governor said that Nigeria required purposeful leadership to achieve sustainable development, adding that he possessed the character, experience and capacity to lead the country. He said that Nigeria had vast arable land and other resources that could transform its economy if properly harnessed. According to him, the country must shift from consumption to production, particularly through agriculture and other productive sectors. On the Federal Government’s borrowing, Obi said taking loans was not inherently wrong but became problematic when the funds were used for consumption rather than productive investments. “It becomes wrong when the government borrows to buy a yacht or a presidential plane for consumption purposes,” he said. He pledged that his administration would ensure transparency in public borrowing, insisting that Nigerians must know why loans were obtained and how the funds would be utilised. On security, the presidential candidate promised to deploy modern technology and other effective measures to tackle insecurity and guarantee the safety of citizens across the country, irrespective of their locations. Obi also vowed that anyone found guilty of corruption, including the president, would face prosecution and imprisonment in accordance with the law. He said his vision was to build a Nigeria where citizens could achieve their aspirations through merit rather than personal connections. “My dream is to see a Nigeria where the son of a nobody can become somebody without knowing anybody,” he added. Obi, who expressed excitement over the turnout at the meeting, described himself as the most credible among the three leading presidential candidates. He cited President Bola Tinubu of the All Progressives Congress (APC), former Vice-President Atiku Abubakar of the African Democratic Congress (ADC) and himself as the leading contenders. He urged Nigerians to participate actively in the forthcoming election and protect their votes. “You should vote for me because I am the most credible candidate among the leading candidates for the presidency,” he said. Obi expressed optimism that Nigeria could achieve meaningful transformation under credible leadership, pledging to provide such leadership if elected. (NAN) The post Obi promises emergency measures on security, corruption, poverty appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Nursing mother drags husband to court over N10,000 ‘breastfeeding allowance’
item.description: A nursing mother, Firdausi Ahmad on Thursday dragged her husband, Malam Anas before a Shari’a Court in Kaduna, seeking divorce and N10,000 monthly for “breastfeeding” allowance. The ​‌‍‍‍‍⁠⁠‍‌‍​‌‌⁠⁠​‌​complainant’s lawyer, Malam Sani Sunusi, told the court that his client had been married to Anas for three years and she was nursing an eight months old daughter. The counsel told the court that his client’s husband, told her to go back to her parents house until he gives her approval to return to their matrimonial home. “Since my client went to her parents, the defendant never checked on her or their eight months old baby. “My client prays the court to dissolve the marriage through Khul’i and is willing to return his dowry of N100,000. “He should also pay N10,000 monthly for the baby’s needs and for the eight months that she’ll be breastfeeding her baby” he prayed. The defendant was not in court. The Judge, Malam Yakubu Abdullahi, adjourned the case until Nov. 11 for the complainant to present her witness or evidence. Abdullahi directed the registrar of the court to send a letter of invitation to the defendant and ensure that he attends the hearing. item.title: Makinde questions Tinubu’s Saudi prayer trip, challenges FG over borrowing
item.description: By Ayobami Okerinde The presidential candidate of the Allied Peoples Movement (APM), Seyi Makinde, has questioned the Federal Government’s decision to seek fresh foreign loans despite rising external reserves and claims of improved revenue collection. Makinde spoke on Thursday at the party’s South-East town hall meeting in Enugu, where he also criticised President Bola Tinubu’s planned trip to Saudi Arabia to pray for Nigeria, urging the government to be transparent about the country’s economic situation. “I was reading on social media yesterday night up until this morning that our president is travelling to Saudi Arabia to pray for Nigeria. Prayers are answered even in this country; we will stay here, and we will pray for Nigeria and also our leaders because Nigeria belongs to all of us,” he said. Makinde’s comments came after the President’s Special Adviser on Information and Strategy, Bayo Onanuga, announced on Wednesday that Tinubu would travel to Makkah on Thursday to perform Umrah, an Islamic pilgrimage, and pray for Nigeria’s peace, unity, stability, and continued progress. The president subsequently departed for the trip on Thursday. Makinde urged the president and his administration to address the country’s challenges honestly, saying prayers should be accompanied by transparency about the state of the economy. “They should pray for Nigeria and stop all the deceit and tell Nigerians the exact true situation of things so that as you are praying, our prayers will not be in vain,” he said. The Oyo State governor also questioned the government’s decision to seek additional borrowing despite claims of improved revenue collection and the country’s growing external reserves. Vanguard reported that President Tinubu recently, in a letter to the Senate, sought the approval of a supplementary external borrowing plan of about $20.52bn and €1.045bn to finance infrastructure and development projects across the country. “They said we have a lot of money in our external reserve and that the Nigeria Revenue Service has surpassed the target for the year, but we still have to go and borrow money. How does it add up?” Makinde asked. He said his experience in the private sector had taught him to assess economic performance by the availability of long-term financing for businesses. “I came from the private sector; at the age of 29, I have paid salaries for workers till today. So, I know when the economy is expanding. One of the indications is that within your economy space you will have long-term facilities,” he said. Makinde added that businesses were largely relying on short-term credit facilities, which he said limited their ability to expand manufacturing and create jobs. He argued that manufacturers could not grow sufficiently when they had to borrow at interest rates of about 25 per cent without access to long-term financing. item.title: Video: Tinubu departs Abuja for Saudi Arabia to perform Umrah
item.description: President Bola Tinubu on Thursday departed Abuja for Makkah, Saudi Arabia, to perform Umrah, an Islamic pilgrimage to the holy city. The presidential aircraft, an Airbus A330-200, took off at 2:20pm local time, with the president expected to return to Nigeria next week after completing the religious exercise. Tinubu was seen off at the airport by six governors: AbdulRahman AbdulRazaq of Kwara, Babagana Zulum of Borno, Uba Sani of Kaduna, Ahmad Aliyu of Sokoto, Umar Namadi of Jigawa and Mai Mala Buni of Yobe. Also present were the Secretary to the Government of the Federation, George Akume; the Attorney-General of the Federation and Minister of Justice, Lateef Fagbemi; and Nigeria’s Ambassador to Mexico, Reno Omokri, alongside other government officials. The President’s departure was announced on Thursday by his Special Assistant on Social Media, Dada Olusegun, in a post on X. Olusegun said the visit would give Tinubu an opportunity for spiritual reflection and prayer for Nigeria. President Bola Ahmed Tinubu departs Abuja for Makkah, Kingdom of Saudi Arabia, to perform Umrah, the Islamic spiritual exercise involving a pilgrimage to the Holy City. The visit gives the President an opportunity for spiritual reflection, devotion, and prayers for Nigeria’s… pic.twitter.com/QFSEFfqpB1 — Daddy D.O (@DOlusegun) October 29, 2026 “The visit gives the President an opportunity for spiritual reflection, devotion, and prayers for Nigeria’s peace, unity, stability, and continued progress,” he wrote. He added that the President would perform the religious rites associated with Umrah while seeking divine guidance for the country. “While in Makkah, President Tinubu will perform the religious rites associated with Umrah, seeking Allah’s guidance and blessings for Nigeria and its people,” Olusegun said. Thursday’s trip marks the second time Tinubu has travelled to Makkah to perform Umrah since assuming office on May 29, 2023. The President visited the holy city in November 2023, shortly after attending the Saudi-African Summit in Riyadh, where he also prayed for divine guidance in leading Nigeria. The latest trip is part of a series of foreign engagements undertaken by Tinubu since becoming president. He has visited more than 30 countries in over 50 unique and recurring trips. item.title: N70,000 Allowance: ‘Negotiate your terms,’ NLC tells TUC
item.description: Joe Ajaero, President of the Nigeria Labour Congress, NLC, has asked the Trade Union Congress, TUC, to negotiate its terms with the Federal Government, as it cannot reject the N70,000 transport allowance NLC agreed with government for public sector workers. Vanguard reported that TUC rejected the proposed N70,000 monthly transport allowance for federal workers, which NLC agreed upon after a meeting. According to TUC, the federal government has the resources to pay N300,000. In a statement by Festus Osifo and Nuhu Toro, President-General and Secretary, respectively, the TUC said in view of the prevailing economic hardship facing workers and the wider population, as well as the proposed measures to address it, what was needed was a salary increase and the implementation of the Joint Health Sector Union, JOHESU, agreement. Read the full story HERE . Responding in an interview on Channels TV on Thursday, Ajaero, NLC President, said officials of the TUC did not negotiate with the federal government on the subject. He described TUC’s position on the allowance as improper. He noted that the leadership of the TUC does not have the power to reject the agreement terms of a sister-agency. The NLC president said: “I would have preferred a situation whereby if NLC was asking for one Naira, TUC will be asking for 10 Naira. “TUC never asked for intervention as a result of the rising cost of transportation. On the issue of asking for wage increase, does the government gift wage increase? There must be a process put in place. “I’m worried for some time now why you will say you reject something that was not given to you. That is not proper. “You don’t have the power to reject what a sister agency negotiates. You have the power to ask for your own.” Vanguard News The post N70,000 Allowance: ‘Negotiate your terms,’ NLC tells TUC appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Tinubu made life expensive, Atiku’ll make it affordable — Akobundu
item.description: By Steve Oko UMUAHIA — The Director-General of the African Democratic Congress (ADC) Presidential Campaign Council, Senator Austin Akobundu, has criticised President Bola Tinubu’s economic policies, saying former Vice-President Atiku Abubakar would prioritise affordability and economic recovery if elected president in 2027. Akobundu spoke during the inauguration of the Atiku/Akobundu Vanguard, a grassroots mobilisation group, in Ikwuano and Umuahia North Local Government Areas of Abia State. The senator, who is also the ADC candidate for Abia Central Senatorial District, expressed confidence in the prospects of Atiku and other party candidates in the 2027 elections, citing what he described as growing public support. “Tinubu has made life expensive for Nigerians. Atiku will make life affordable again for the people,” he said. Akobundu said Atiku’s economic proposals, including the restoration of targeted subsidies, would help ease financial pressures on Nigerians and support economic recovery. He also highlighted the former vice-president’s positions on national unity and equal opportunities, arguing that the proposed revival of the Eastern maritime port corridor could stimulate trade, investment and economic activities in the South-East. The senator urged Nigerians, particularly those in the South-East, to support Atiku, whom he described as capable of improving living conditions and strengthening the economy. He further urged the region to look beyond political sentiments, arguing that Atiku’s presidency could create opportunities for a Nigerian of Igbo extraction to emerge as president in the future. Constituency projects, legislative interventions Akobundu also highlighted his legislative activities and constituency projects in Ikwuano and Umuahia North, including efforts to attract federal institutions, youth empowerment programmes, scholarships, student grants, healthcare interventions and infrastructure development. He cited his intervention on the delayed rehabilitation of the Umuahia–Ikot Ekpene Federal Road, saying the Senate had acted on his motion before the Abia State Government took over the reconstruction under a refund arrangement with the Federal Government. The senator commended Governor Alex Otti for taking over the project and the quality of work carried out, while acknowledging the contributions of former lawmaker, Rep. Sam Onuigbo, to efforts to secure the road’s rehabilitation. “I do not play politics of division and bitterness. That road is for our people, and anyone who contributes to its reconstruction deserves commendation,” he said. Youth empowerment, education The senator listed scholarships, student grants, vocational training and digital skills development among his human capital development initiatives. item.title: NAFDAC secures five-year jail term for fake Goya oil manufacturer
item.description: ….Court gives Aba businessman option of ₦5m fine By Chioma Obinna The National Agency for Food and Drug Administration and Control (NAFDAC) has secured the conviction of a businessman in Aba, Abia State, for manufacturing and selling counterfeit Goya Extra Virgin Olive Oil, sentencing him to five years’ imprisonment with an option of a ₦5 million fine. The conviction, which followed months of investigation and prosecution, marks a major enforcement action against food counterfeiting and the growing threat posed by falsified products to unsuspecting Nigerian consumers. The businessman, Mr Innocent Okoye, Managing Director of Chikason Industrial Nigeria Limited, Aba, was convicted on two counts relating to the manufacture and sale of counterfeit Goya Extra Virgin Olive Oil. Justice K. O. Ogundare of the Federal High Court, Umuahia, Abia State, delivered the judgment on Wednesday, October 28, 2026, according to information released by NAFDAC. The case arose from an enforcement operation conducted by the agency’s Investigation and Enforcement Directorate in April 2026, during which officials uncovered a facility in Aba allegedly used for the production and distribution of counterfeit Goya oil. NAFDAC arrested the suspect and forwarded samples of the recovered products to its laboratory for scientific analysis. The investigation subsequently led to criminal proceedings against Okoye and his eventual conviction on the two counts. The development comes amid growing concerns over the circulation of fake food products in Nigerian markets, with counterfeiters allegedly exploiting the popularity of established brands to deceive consumers and profit from products whose composition and safety cannot be guaranteed. In January 2026, NAFDAC raised the alarm over counterfeit Goya oil packaged in polyethylene terephthalate (PET) plastic bottles and sold to unsuspecting consumers as genuine imported products. At a media briefing in Lagos, the agency’s Director of Investigation and Enforcement, Dr Martins Iluyomade, disclosed that investigators had uncovered an illegal production operation at Oke-Arin Market, Idumota, Lagos. According to the agency, operators of the facility were allegedly processing palm oil with colouring agents before repackaging the mixture as Goya oil for sale. Iluyomade explained that genuine Goya oil authorised for sale in Nigeria was imported in original glass bottles through approved distribution channels. He warned consumers to be wary of products bearing the brand name in PET plastic bottles. The warning highlighted the difficulties consumers face in distinguishing genuine products from counterfeits, particularly when imitation goods are packaged and marketed to resemble established brands. item.title: LAUTECH ASUU begins indefinite strike
item.description: By Adeola Badru Academic activities have been disrupted at Ladoke Akintola University of Technology (LAUTECH), Ogbomoso, Oyo State, following the commencement of an indefinite strike by the institution’s chapter of the Academic Staff Union of Universities (ASUU) on Thursday. The industrial action followed the expiration of a 14-day ultimatum issued by the union to the university management over outstanding demands, including the implementation of the 2025 Federal Government of Nigeria (FGN)-ASUU Agreement and the payment of consequential arrears dating back to January 2026. The union is also demanding the immediate payment of outstanding Earned Academic Allowances (EAA) and promotion arrears covering the period from 2013 to 2025. According to ASUU, the university’s Governing Council formally accepted and approved the implementation of the December 2025 FGN-ASUU Agreement. However, the union said the management had repeatedly cited a lack of funds as the reason for delays in implementation. Beyond the financial demands, the union is seeking the resolution of several administrative and governance issues before the Vice-Chancellor and the university management. These include concerns about the composition of the Staff Disciplinary Committee, the reconstitution of the Committee of Provosts and Deans, and transparency in the university’s electronic voting system. In a statement jointly signed by the branch Chairperson, Prof. Olujimi Dada, and the Secretary, Dr Soji Arinola, the union expressed frustration over the failure to resolve the issues despite repeated attempts at formal and informal dialogue. The union said it decided to embark on the indefinite strike after exhausting several avenues of engagement without reaching a resolution. It urged members to remain united throughout the industrial action and advised them to disregard information or directives not issued directly by the branch chairperson. The union stressed that only information and directives issued by the branch chairperson should be treated as authentic during the strike. item.title: 2027: INEC moves to address electoral risks in Ebonyi
item.description: By Jeff Agbodo, Abakaliki The Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) in Ebonyi State has intensified efforts to identify and address potential risks that could disrupt the conduct of the 2027 general elections. The move followed a workshop on Electoral Risk Management organised at the commission’s headquarters in Abakaliki for stakeholders, including media representatives, security agencies and local government electoral officers. Participants identified potential threats to the elections, including snatching and destruction of electoral materials, abduction of election officials and the inaccessibility of some villages and communities. Speaking at the workshop, INEC Administrative Secretary in Ebonyi State, Mrs Joan Onyibor, said the exercise was timely given the proximity of the January and February 2027 elections. She explained that electoral risk management provided a structured and proactive approach to identifying, assessing, monitoring and mitigating threats that could compromise the electoral process. According to her, such risks could include security threats, political tensions, misinformation, environmental challenges, logistical constraints and other operational difficulties. Onyibor warned that failure to identify and address the risks could disrupt electoral activities, endanger voters and election officials, and undermine public confidence in the electoral process. Declaring the workshop open, the Resident Electoral Commissioner (REC) in Ebonyi State, Mrs Pauline Ugochi Onyeka, commended the Head of Planning and Monitoring, Mrs Mercy Amechi-Okorie, for organising the programme for stakeholders. Onyeka said strengthening the electoral risk management framework had become increasingly important as the 2027 elections approached. “We must move beyond responding to challenges only after they emerge and adopt a proactive approach that allows us to anticipate risks and address them before they develop into serious threats,” she said. She added that the workshop was designed to improve stakeholders’ understanding of electoral risk management, build institutional capacity and strengthen their ability to identify, document and report potential threats across different locations. The REC stressed that effective electoral risk management depended on close cooperation and timely information-sharing among INEC offices, security agencies, civil society organisations, the media and other stakeholders. “No institution can manage every electoral risk effectively on its own,” Onyeka said, calling for a coordinated approach to strengthen preparedness and response mechanisms. She said collaboration among stakeholders would help improve the security and integrity of the electoral process ahead of the 2027 general elections. item.title: Reps seek review of NCC phone rules over price hike fears
item.description: By Gift Chapi Odekina, Abuja The House of Representatives has called for a review of the Nigerian Communications Commission’s (NCC) mobile device verification requirements over concerns that the policy could increase phone prices and lead to the wrongful blocking of legitimate used devices. The House warned that additional compliance costs under the framework could increase expenses for phone importers and retailers, with consumers, particularly low-income Nigerians, likely to bear the burden through higher prices. The resolution followed a motion sponsored by a Kano lawmaker, Sani Wakili, urging the commission to review the implementation of its device verification framework in consultation with relevant stakeholders. The framework, operated through the Device Management System and the Central Equipment Identity Register, enables the identification and verification of mobile phones and other SIM-enabled devices using their International Mobile Equipment Identity (IMEI) numbers. Lawmakers noted that the enhanced verification requirements, which took effect on October 7, 2026, impose additional compliance obligations on newly imported devices, potentially raising operating costs for importers and retailers. They expressed concern that businesses could transfer the additional expenses to consumers, making mobile phones less affordable for Nigerians who rely on them for communication, education, banking and other commercial activities. The House also raised concerns about possible technical errors, database mismatches and limitations in the commission’s scanning and verification systems, warning that such challenges could result in legitimate devices being wrongly rejected or blocked. According to the lawmakers, the second-hand phone market could be particularly affected, given that used devices offer a more affordable alternative to new phones for many Nigerians. While acknowledging the NCC’s efforts to tackle counterfeit, cloned and stolen mobile phones, the House stressed that enforcement should not unfairly penalise legitimate businesses or restrict access to affordable communication devices. Consequently, the lawmakers urged the commission to review the framework’s implementation, simplify verification procedures and reduce compliance costs. They also called for a fair and accessible verification process for used and second-hand mobile phones to prevent legitimate devices from being wrongly flagged or blocked. To further examine the concerns, the House mandated its Committees on Communications and Commerce to engage the NCC and other relevant stakeholders on the implementation of the requirements and report back within four weeks for further legislative action. The Committee on Legislative Compliance was also directed to ensure compliance with the resolution. item.title: ‘I won’t waste my time talking about Amaechi’ — Oshiomhole
item.description: Senator Adams Oshiomhole has dismissed former Rivers State Governor Rotimi Amaechi as unreliable, saying he would not waste his time discussing the former minister. Oshiomhole spoke on TVC while reacting to Amaechi’s comments that President Bola Tinubu faces more challengers in the 2027 presidential election top challengers are from the South, while former Vice-President Atiku Abubakar has fewer opponents because he is from the North. “If you know Amaechi, you won’t waste airtime talking about him,” Oshiomhole said. The former Edo State governor questioned Amaechi’s political consistency, citing his past dispute with Atiku over the African Democratic Congress presidential primary. According to Oshiomhole, Amaechi had accused Atiku of emerging from a fraudulent primary and challenged his victory in court. “Here is Amaechi on record in your TVC coverage and other network stations, who said that his own boss, the presidential candidate Atiku Abubakar, that the primary that produce him was a fraudulent process, and Atiku stole the mandate, he didn’t win the mandate. He didn’t stop there. Amaechi went to court to challenge Atiku that he stole the mandate,” he said. Oshiomhole added that Atiku later reached an agreement with Amaechi, claiming the former vice-president had asked him to share the mandate they allegedly obtained through a fraudulent process. “This is not social media, there are court documents, and Atiku went back to him and said okay, let’s share the stolen mandate together,” he said. Oshiomhole also referred to Amaechi’s political history, arguing that his rise to power and appointment as a minister were not the result of direct electoral victories. He said Amaechi became governor following a Supreme Court decision and was appointed minister by former President Muhammadu Buhari in 2015. “And I am not surprised that knowing what I know about him…he’s been very lucky that Supreme Court make him a governor without appearing on the ballot, and President Buhari made him a minister without voting for him in 2015, because I was a national player and later national chairman, so I know what I’m talking about,” Oshiomhole said. The senator further criticised Amaechi for describing other political figures as ethnic champions, arguing that the former governor had presented himself as the exception before the African Democratic Congress primaries. “He referred to Atiku as an ethnic champion. He referred to every other person as an ethnic champion. He was the only non-ethnic champion in the ADC before their primaries,” Oshiomhole said. He questioned Amaechi’s assessment of other political leaders, saying someone who dismisses others as ethnic champions should not be taken seriously when discussing leadership in a diverse country like Nigeria. item.title: 2027: INEC fears poll disruption in insecure areas
item.description: By Ben Ngwakwe, Gombe The Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) has raised concerns that insecurity could disrupt or prevent the conduct of the 2027 general elections in some parts of the country. INEC Chairman, Prof. Joash Amupitan, SAN, expressed the concern on Tuesday in Gombe while addressing participants at the North-East Zonal Interactive Staff Meeting and Operational Readiness Assessment for the 2027 general elections. Amupitan described insecurity in some parts of the country as a major challenge to the conduct of credible elections, calling for urgent and coordinated action by security agencies to protect the electoral process. He said he would engage the National Security Adviser, the Chief of Army Staff and other senior security officials upon his return to Abuja to discuss measures to address the threats and create a safer environment for the elections. The INEC chairman said the commission would adopt a proactive approach to electoral security rather than wait for threats to escalate before responding. He added that INEC was strengthening collaboration with the Nigeria Police Force, the Nigeria Security and Civil Defence Corps, the Department of State Services, the Armed Forces and other relevant agencies through the Inter-Agency Consultative Committee on Election Security (ICCES). According to him, the collaboration is designed to improve intelligence-sharing, security coordination and operational preparedness ahead of the 2027 polls. The concerns come as INEC intensifies preparations for the elections, with insecurity posing potential risks to the movement of electoral personnel, distribution of sensitive election materials and participation of voters in affected communities. Amupitan stressed that sustained cooperation between electoral authorities and security agencies would be critical to ensuring that Nigerians could exercise their democratic rights without fear or intimidation. He said early intervention, effective deployment of security personnel and a coordinated response to security threats were necessary to prevent insecurity from undermining the credibility, inclusiveness and peaceful conduct of the 2027 general elections. item.title: Neville warns managers can need sacking ‘for their own good’ as Carrick fights on
item.description: Gary Neville says managers sometimes need to dismissed “for their own good” as Manchester United persist with under-pressure boss Michael Carrick. Carrick’s future at Old Trafford has been the subject of intense speculation after a miserable run of eight games without a win. Sunday’s 3-0 humbling at home to Bournemouth left the English giants one point above the Premier League relegation zone. United have won just two of 12 matches in all competitions this season, with a return of seven points from eight league games representing their worst start to a league season in 40 years. But former United and England midfielder Carrick, 45, remains in charge and is expected to give a pre-match press conference later Thursday ahead of the team’s league match away to Chelsea on Saturday. “I reckon what’s happened in the 24 hours after Bournemouth is that they (the United hierarchy) literally debated it (Carrick’s future) back and forth,” former Manchester United captain Neville said on the Stick to Football podcast. “I don’t know this, but they’ve debated it to the point where they’ve got themselves into a muddle, and thought, ‘we’ll just stay with him’. “I think staying with him is a result of the lack of planning, the lack of probably available options, the lack of decision-making around the two people that probably are available. That’s when you’re really struggling.” Neville, a former United team-mate of Carrick, added: “Sometimes a manager needs sacking for their own good. I needed sacking at Valencia. I was happy that they put me out of my misery.” – ‘Enough is enough’ – Both Eddie Howe, previously in charge of Newcastle, and former Germany boss Julian Nagelsmann have been touted as possible replacements for Carrick at Old Trafford. Carrick, however, appears to have the backing of the United faithful, being warmly applauded by fans as he made his way down the tunnel following the defeat by Bournemouth. Moments later a chorus of boos erupted as the players left the pitch as supporters made clear where they think the blame lies for United’s current malaise. Carrick was handed a two-year deal in May after inspiring an impressive revival following the team’s struggles under Ruben Amorim — United secured third place in the Premier League and a return to the Champions League. The drastic decline this season is an all-too-familiar story for United supporters, who last witnessed a Premier League title triumph 13 years ago under Alex Ferguson. Neville believes the root of United’s woes is majority owners the Glazer family, saying “enough is enough” as he urged them to sell-up. item.title: Tinubu has broken Imo’s shackles — Okorocha hails court judgment
item.description: Former Imo State Governor Rochas Okorocha has praised President Bola Tinubu following a Federal High Court judgment recognising him as the All Progressives Congress candidate for Imo West Senatorial District, saying the ruling has broken the shackles holding the state. Okorocha spoke on Thursday while hosting his legal team after the judgment delivered by Justice Obiora Egwuatu of the Federal High Court in Abuja. The court ruled that Okorocha won the APC senatorial primary conducted on May 18, 2026, and ordered the party to submit his name to the Independent National Electoral Commission as its candidate for the January 16, 2027 senatorial election. The court also directed Governor Hope Uzodimma to stop parading himself as the party’s candidate. Reacting to the judgment, Okorocha thanked the judiciary for standing on the side of justice, describing the outcome as a victory for the people of Imo State. “I thank the judiciary for standing on the side of justice. I could imagine what would have happened in the state if they decided to twist justice. This is a victory for Imo State,” he said. The former governor also linked the judgment to the symbolic shackle on Tinubu’s traditional cap, suggesting that the President’s position had become clearer through the court’s decision. “This is also the first time the Imo people will understand the sign of the shackle on President Tinubu’s cap. By this judgment, the shackle on Imo State has been broken, and it is also evident that the President is tired of this nonsense and that he is not in support of it,” Okorocha said. He expressed gratitude to Tinubu, although he did not provide direct evidence that the President had intervened in the legal dispute or influenced the court’s decision. The judgment followed a legal battle in which Okorocha challenged INEC’s recognition of Uzodimma as the APC’s candidate for Imo West. The dispute attracted further attention earlier this month after INEC petitioned the police and the Department of State Services over a disputed document circulating online that purported to name Okorocha as the winner of the primary. INEC maintained that its official report recognised Uzodimma as the winner. Okorocha also addressed reports surrounding his alleged arrest, saying he deliberately refrained from commenting when the news broke. “When the news broke out that I was arrested, I refused to make any comments,” he said. He, however, questioned the documents presented during the dispute over the APC primary, particularly the claims that Uzodimma emerged through consensus and the discrepancies he alleged in the dates recorded in the documents. Okorocha questioned how a document could indicate that Uzodimma emerged through consensus when, according to him, individual scores were recorded. item.title: ‘Horrific’ Russian Drone Strike Kills 14 At Ukraine Train Station
item.description: A Russian drone slammed into a busy platform at a railway station in Ukraine’s Dnipro on Thursday killing at least 14 people in what President Volodymyr Zelensky called a “horrific” attack that demands a response from Kyiv’s allies. The strike came as Ukraine and Russia strive to uphold a fragile local ceasefire in the ravaged city of Oleshky — under Russian occupation since 2022 and where residents have faced months of food, water and medicine shortages. The truce was holding into its third day, both countries said, with the Ukrainian human rights ombudsman Dmytro Lubinets announcing that he had “set out with the Ukrainian delegation towards Oleshky” through Belarus and Russia. But elsewhere, Moscow continued to pummel Ukraine. The strike at the Dnipro train station hit a platform “where a regular commuter train and a regular passenger train were standing”, Zelensky said. By early Thursday afternoon, Dnipropetrovsk regional governor Oleksandr Ganzha said the death toll from the strike had risen to 14. (Photo by Handout / UKRAINIAN EMERGENCY SERVICE / AFP) Another 14 had been wounded, he said, adding that six of them were in severe condition after suffering “multiple shrapnel wounds”, including an 11-year-old boy and a man who had “both legs amputated”. Zelensky slammed the attack as “horrific” and insisted that “sanctions against Moscow and its war machine must not be eased for as long as this Russian war continues”. Images released by Ukrainian emergency services showed bodies on the platform, rescuers helping victims to safety and two burnt-out passenger trains with their windows shattered. French President Emmanuel Macron reacted with outrage to the attack, stressing the need for “far more than a localised ceasefire” like the one in Oleshky. “It is intolerable that Russia continues to reject all proposals to this end, choosing instead to pursue escalation and target civilians,” he said on X. Zelensky slams sanctions relief Russia has fired drones on trains across Ukraine since the first days of its 2022 invasion — destroying hundreds of locomotives and killing several railway workers. Ukraine’s air force said it had intercepted three jet-powered drones in a daytime attack, but that a fourth evaded its defences and hit the station. In the aftermath of the attack, Zelensky refreshed his criticism of a deal struck this month between US President Donald Trump and his Russian counterpart Vladimir Putin to ease some sanctions on Russia allowing Moscow to release diesel onto global markets. “How many such terrorist strikes has Russia carried out against our people since sanctions were lifted on some Russian oligarchs and the energy sector, instead of de-escalating,” he asked. item.title: Meet Nigerian Engineer Yinka Ogunbiyi behind machine that braids hair five times faster
item.description: By Enitan Abdultawab Nigerian-born engineer Yinka Ogunbiyi is gaining attention for developing HaloBraid, an automated hair braiding device designed to help professional stylists complete hairstyles up to five times faster while reducing the physical strain associated with hours of braiding. Ogunbiyi, a Harvard graduate and biomechanical engineer, recently demonstrated how the technology works, offering a glimpse into how automation could transform the hair and beauty industry, particularly protective hairstyles that often require several hours to complete. Unlike a machine that replaces the stylist entirely, HaloBraid is designed to work alongside professional hairdressers. The stylist first sections the hair, applies the necessary products and starts the braid by hand before feeding it into the device. The machine then handles the repetitive weaving along the length of the hair, allowing the stylist to finish and seal the ends. The innovation aims to reduce the time spent on braiding while easing the physical demands placed on stylists who spend long hours working with clients. It also seeks to improve the salon experience without removing the human skill involved in creating the final hairstyle. Ogunbiyi said the inspiration for the invention came from her personal experience of getting her hair braided from childhood and the challenges she repeatedly observed among both stylists and clients. “My braid story starts at age four, sitting between my mum’s legs as she braided my hair for the first time. Since then, I’ve spent thousands of hours getting my hair braided — and heard the same story from stylists and clients again and again: braiding is beautiful, but it takes too much time and too much strain,” she said. Drawing on her background in biomechanical engineering, Ogunbiyi said she recognised the need for a better approach and developed HaloBraid in collaboration with hairstylists, designers and other professionals. She added that the device was built with people close to her in mind, including her mother, hairstylists and aunties, as well as others around the world who understand the experience of spending hours in a salon chair. The venture has also attracted significant investor interest, securing $7 million in seed funding in a round led by Seven Seven Six, the venture capital firm founded by Reddit co founder Alexis Ohanian, who is married to tennis champion Serena Williams. The development adds to Ogunbiyi’s growing recognition in innovation and entrepreneurship. Her HaloBraid project previously won a $75,000 Harvard Innovation Prize, highlighting the potential of the technology to address a familiar challenge in the beauty industry. With its latest demonstration, HaloBraid is positioning itself as a technology that combines traditional hairstyling expertise with automation, potentially giving stylists more time to serve clients while reducing the repetitive work involved in braiding. item.title: Indonesians Celebrate Rain After Months Of Smoke And Suffering
item.description: Residents and firefighters in an Indonesian city long shrouded in a toxic haze brought on by months of wildfires rushed outside dancing and chanting as rain this week brought a welcome respite. On Wednesday night, exhausted volunteer firefighters jumped around in the puddles and kissed the ground in gratitude as another burst came down. “We were overjoyed; every one of us volunteers was so happy that we prostrated ourselves in gratitude. Praise be to God that there was finally rain,” firefighter Lukman El Hakim told AFP. TOPSHOT – Indonesian soldiers, tasked with fighting forest and land fires, celebrate as it rains in Banjar Baru, South Kalimantan province on October 28, 2026, following months of forest and land fires. (Photo by MUDA SAGALA / AFP) | MUDA SAGALA / AFP Intermittent rains have been falling in Palangkaraya, the capital of Central Kalimantan province on Indonesian Borneo, where devastating wildfires have raged since August. The city’s air quality index hit 4,000 this month, its worst ever measurement and more than 13 times the environment ministry’s threshold for pollution deemed “hazardous” to health. More than 11,000 people have been treated for respiratory infections in Palangkaraya during the months-long crisis that has also affected Indonesia’s neighbours with haze pollution. The World Health Organisation has linked exposure to air pollution, including high levels of tiny, airborne PM2.5 particles, to increased risk of illness and premature death. item.title: 2027: Abia CP warns politicians against violence, intimidation
item.description: …Orders parties to notify police before rallies . We ‘re for nobody, we ‘re for everybody – REC, urges candidates to accept results or seek redress in court By Steve Oko UMUAHIA – The Abia State Commissioner of Police, CP Wilfred Afolabi, has warned political parties and their supporters against violence, intimidation, inflammatory statements and destruction of property ahead of the 2027 general elections. This is as the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) has declared its neutrality in the 2027 Abia governorship election, assuring all candidates that it will provide a level playing field for every contestant. CP Afolabi, who spoke at the signing of a peace accord involving the NEC, security agencies and political parties in Umuahia, urged parties to notify the police in writing before holding rallies, processions and other political activities to enable adequate security arrangements. The meeting, held at the Police Officers’ Mess, Umuahia, was attended by INEC’s Resident Electoral Commissioner in Abia, Prof. Sylvia Agu, heads of sister security agencies and representatives of registered political parties and campaign teams. The Police boss reaffirmed the command’s commitment to providing professional, impartial and adequate security for all candidates, parties and their supporters, irrespective of political affiliation. He disclosed that the command had strengthened its security architecture through intelligence gathering and analysis, crime mapping, the revamp of its Cybercrime Unit and improved operational response mechanisms. Afolabi also acknowledged Governor Alex Otti’s directive on adequate security for political campaigns and related activities. He pledged continued collaboration with INEC, other security agencies and political stakeholders to protect lives and property and ensure a peaceful electoral process. The peace accord, which followed a review of relevant electoral laws by the command’s legal officer, was subsequently read to the stakeholders before representatives of political parties signed individually, pledging to pursue their political ambitions peacefully. Speaking at the event, the REC, Prof. Agu, said the commission was committed to serving all candidates equally, irrespective of their political parties, while urging them to maintain peace before, during and after the election. “We are not working for any particular party; we are working for all of you here. We are going to deliver on our mandate, but we are asking you to conduct yourselves properly,” she said. The REC urged candidates to accept the outcome of a free, fair and credible election, advising those dissatisfied with the results to seek redress through the judiciary rather than resort to violence or discredit the electoral process. She stressed that electoral contests inevitably produce winners and losers, urging candidates to demonstrate sportsmanship regardless of the outcome. “In any contest, there must be a winner and a loser. However, a Punch analysis estimates that the programme could cost ₦465.7 billion over six months if all 1.1 million employee records on the federal payroll qualify. This is an estimate, not an officially approved expenditure figure. TUC President Festus Osifo argues that earlier temporary wage awards were inconsistently implemented and failed to reach many eligible workers. Why it matters: What appeared to be a breakthrough in labour negotiations has exposed disagreement within organised labour. Affected candidates include Isa Pantami of the PDP in Gombe, Ladi Adebutu of the PDP in Ogun and Aminu Gwarzo of the Nigeria Democratic Congress in Kano.
